texts.error.demo.axis_not_active: Tic %1: %2 is %3, and the core's controller has no such input active.
texts.error.demo.axis_out_of_range: Tic %1: %2 is %3, outside the core's %4 to %5.
texts.error.demo.button_not_active: Tic %1: %2 is pressed, and the core's controller has no such input active.
texts.error.demo.dsda_header_newer: Its DSDA header is version %1, newer than dsda-doom 0.30's (3).
texts.error.demo.extended_header_unknown: Its extended header (version byte 255) is neither dsda's nor PrBoom+um's.
texts.error.demo.footer_iwad_of_no_game: Its footer's IWAD, %1, is the IWAD of none of the games the core plays.
texts.error.demo.heretic_artifact_flags: Tic %1: Heretic's artifact byte %2 has Hexen's flags.
texts.error.demo.hexen_class: Player %1's class is %2. Hexen's are 0 to 2.
texts.error.demo.hexen_extended_jump: Tic %1: an extended jump in Hexen, which jumps with its artifact flag.
texts.error.demo.hexen_warp: Hexen's -warp %1 goes to map %2, not the demo's %3: the core starts a game by its warp number.
texts.error.demo.iwad_of_no_game: %1 is the IWAD of none of the games the core plays: its name and its lumps say none.
texts.error.demo.key_frame: It starts from a key frame (a saved game inside the demo). A movie starts with the game.
texts.error.demo.longtics_doom: Longtics are for Heretic and Hexen demos. A Doom demo's format says its turning.
texts.error.demo.mbf21_comp_flags: Its MBF21 options name %1 compatibility flags. dsda-doom 0.30 knows 25.
texts.error.demo.more_than_four_players: Players %1 are in the game. The core has four.
texts.error.demo.no_mapinfo: There is no MAPINFO in the IWAD or the PWADs: Hexen's maps are reached by their warp numbers.
texts.error.demo.no_player: No player is in the game.
texts.error.demo.no_version_byte: Its header has no version byte, and it could be a demo of any of these: %1. Say the game (its IWAD, or its release).
texts.error.demo.no_version_byte_none: Its header has no version byte, and it is a demo of none of Doom 1.2, Heretic or Hexen.
texts.error.demo.other_game_iwad: It is a %1 demo, and %2 is %3's IWAD.
texts.error.demo.saves_or_loads: Tic %1 saves or loads a game (dsda's casual extended commands). A movie cannot.
texts.error.demo.signature_203_unknown: Its version 203 signature is neither LxDoom's nor MBF's.
texts.error.demo.umapinfo_header_unknown: Its PrBoom+um extended header is not the one dsda-doom knows.
texts.error.demo.version_unknown: Its version byte %1 is no demo format dsda-doom knows.
texts.error.demo.which_iwad: The demo does not say which IWAD it is for: give its IWAD.
texts.error.demo.which_iwad_footer: The demo does not say which IWAD it is for beyond its footer's name, %1, which is %2: give its IWAD.
texts.error.demo_options_complevel_has_none: The setting demoOptions is the option block of a demo for Boom or later. Compatibility level %1 has none.
texts.error.demo_options_not_hex: The setting demoOptions is not hexadecimal (two digits a byte).
texts.error.demo_options_size: The setting demoOptions is %1 bytes. The option block of compatibility level %2 is %3.
texts.error.demo_options_size.mbf21: 21 bytes and its compatibility flags (at most 46)
texts.error.import.no_demo: There is no demo: the file "movie" is not mounted.
texts.error.needs_its_iwad: %1 needs its IWAD, %2 (firmware), which is not there.
texts.error.no_player_present: No player is present (the settings player1Present to player4Present).
texts.error.scale_factor_range: The setting scaleFactor is %1. It goes from 1 to 12.
texts.error.scale_factor_too_large: scaleFactor %1 at %2 is %3x%4, larger than the core's %5x%6.
texts.error.setting_game_is_none: The setting game is "%1", which is none of the games the core knows.
texts.firmware.iwad.about: %1 is the game. Any release of it can be used, and so can a modified IWAD. You have to supply it. The package contains none of the game's data. The project records exactly which file it was, and the compatibility level decides which release's rules the game follows.
texts.import.fast.about: For a demo that was recorded with -fast. The headers of Doom 1.0 to 1.2, Heretic and Hexen demos do not hold this. A later Doom demo format holds its own flag.
texts.import.longtics.about: For a Heretic or Hexen demo that was recorded with -longtics but whose header does not say so (demos from Hexen+, before vvHeretic added a header flag). Its turns are then read as 16-bit values. A demo whose header says so needs nothing.
texts.import.nomonsters.about: For a demo that was recorded with -nomonsters but whose header does not say so. Demos of Doom 1.0 to 1.2 hold no monster flags, and Heretic and Hexen demos hold them only when DSDA-Doom recorded them. A later Doom demo format holds its own flags.
texts.import.nopwads.about: Uses none of the PWADs and patches named in the demo's footer. It is for the IWADs' own demos, which were recorded with a fix that is now part of the IWAD.
texts.import.pwads: PWADs and patches, in load order
texts.import.respawn.about: For a demo that was recorded with -respawn but whose header does not say so. Demos of Doom 1.0 to 1.2 hold no monster flags, and Heretic and Hexen demos hold them only when DSDA-Doom recorded them. A later Doom demo format holds its own flags.
texts.note.footer_files_not_taken: Its footer names %1. None were taken (No PWADs).
texts.note.footer_no_pwad_needed: Its footer names no PWAD the core needs.
texts.note.no_end_marker: It has no end marker: its tics run to the file's end, as dsda plays them.
texts.note.no_monster_flags: A 1.2 demo does not hold its monster flags, so none were assumed. Respawn, fast and no monsters can be set in the import options.
texts.property.ammo: Player 1's ammo, by type (am_clip, am_shell, am_cell, am_misl)
texts.property.game_skill: gameskill (0: I'm too young to die .. 4: Nightmare!)
texts.property.level_exit_reached: The level's exit was reached this tic (with preventLevelExit, and not taken)
texts.property.level_game_end_reached: The game's end was reached this tic
texts.property.level_things: The things on the level (the Things domain's records)
texts.property.machine_halted: The engine stopped on an error
texts.property.machine_lag: The last step was the screen melt's, the game waiting
texts.property.machine_steps: Steps since power-on: one tic each
texts.property.rng_index: rndindex: P_Random's, the game's (vanilla's table index)
texts.property.rng_misc_index: prndindex: M_Random's (pr_misc - the status bar's face, the menus; not the game's)
texts.setting.alwaysrun.about: Whether the player always runs, with the slower walking speed not available. This reproduces a bug in the original Doom: setting the joystick run button to an invalid high number makes the game treat it as always pressed.
texts.setting.chainepisodes.about: Finishing one episode leads to the next without a break. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.compatibilitylevel.about: The version of Doom, or of one of its ports, whose behaviour this movie follows. The highest level that is compatible with the original game is 'Final Doom'. Newer WADs may need a higher level. DSDA-Doom used alone defaults to MBF21, which supports the features of all lower levels but is the furthest from the original game.
texts.setting.coopspawns.about: Plays a single-player game with the monsters and items that the cooperative mode places.
texts.setting.demooptions.about: The game options stored in the header of a demo made for Boom or a later port, written as hexadecimal. They are the 64 bytes of Boom, MBF and PrBoom, or the 21 bytes of MBF21 followed by its compatibility flags. They cover monster memory, friction, pushers, bobbing, demo insurance, infighting, helper dogs and their distance, the monsters' behaviour and the compatibility flags. When this is empty, the defaults of the compatibility level and a PWAD's OPTIONS lump are used, as DSDA-Doom records them. The monster flags and the seed are taken from the settings, not from this value.
texts.setting.displaycommands.about: Shows the recent inputs on the screen. The last 10 are kept, and empty inputs are left out. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.displaycoordinates.about: Shows the player's position, angle, speed and distance travelled per frame. The colour shows the kind of movement: green for SR40, blue for SR50, red for turbo or wallrun. The original game has this through the IDMYPOS cheat code, but it shows only the angle, X and Y.
texts.setting.displayplayer.about: Which player's point of view the picture is drawn from (1 to 4). If that player is not present, the first player who is present is used.
texts.setting.dsdaexhud.about: Shows DSDA-Doom's own information above the original heads-up display. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.emulateprboom.about: Plays the way an older PrBoom+ did (DSDA-Doom's -emulate option, with a version such as 2.5.0.8), which the footer of a demo may ask for. When this is empty, the game plays as DSDA-Doom does.
texts.setting.extendedcommands.about: DSDA-Doom's extended commands, which its own DSDA demo format holds: jumping and free look, and, with the casual features, god mode and walking through walls. It is off for every other demo format.
texts.setting.fastmonsters.about: Makes monsters move and attack much faster. It is always on at the Nightmare! difficulty.
texts.setting.fullvision.about: Removes all darkness. The original game has this through the IDBEHOLDL cheat code.
texts.setting.game.about: Which game the machine is (Chimera's System). It is the game the IWAD belongs to. It is not shown on the settings page.
texts.setting.gamma.about: Makes the picture brighter (0 to 4). The original game's default is "OFF" (0). The Change Gamma button steps through the values.
texts.setting.initialepisode.about: The episode the game starts in. It is ignored for IWADs without episodes (for example DOOM2) and for Shareware.
texts.setting.initialmap.about: The map the game starts in.
texts.setting.internalaspect.about: The shape of the picture the game draws. 'Native' is a multiple of 320x200, and Chimera stretches it to 4:3, much like the original game. The other choices draw a picture that already has the right shape. That is useful for viewing the Automap at higher resolutions, because it avoids the distorted pixels that stretching afterwards causes.
texts.setting.mapcoordinates.about: Shows the coordinates within the level on the Automap. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.mapdetails.about: Shows all lines (linedefs) and things on the Automap. The original game has this through the IDDT cheat code.
texts.setting.mapoverlay.about: Shows the Automap on top of the game view. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.maptime.about: Shows the elapsed time on the Automap. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.maptotals.about: Shows the counts of kills, items and secrets on the Automap. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.maptrail.about: Shows the player's earlier positions as a trail when Automap Details is on. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.maptrailsize.about: How many earlier positions are shown as a trail on the Automap (1 to 350).
texts.setting.monstersrespawn.about: Makes monsters come back to life shortly after dying. It is always on at the Nightmare! difficulty.
texts.setting.mouserunsensitivity.about: How fast the player runs when the mouse is used.
texts.setting.mouseturnsensitivity.about: How fast the player turns when the mouse is used.
texts.setting.multiplayermode.about: Which multiplayer mode the game is played in.
texts.setting.musicvolume.about: The volume of the music (0 to 15).
texts.setting.nomonsters.about: Removes all monsters from the level.
texts.setting.overrundonut.about: Reproduces the original game's donut overflow bug (the overrun_donut_emulate option, which is off by default).
texts.setting.overrunintercept.about: Reproduces the original game's intercepts overflow bug (the overrun_intercept_emulate option, which is on by default).
texts.setting.overrunmissedbackside.about: Reproduces the original game's missed backside overflow bug (the overrun_missedbackside_emulate option, which is off by default).
texts.setting.overrunplayeringame.about: Reproduces the original game's playeringame overflow bug (the overrun_playeringame_emulate option, which is on by default).
texts.setting.overrunreject.about: Reproduces the original game's REJECT overflow bug (the overrun_reject_emulate option, which is on by default).
texts.setting.overrunspechit.about: Reproduces the original game's spechit overflow bug (DSDA-Doom's overrun_spechit_emulate option, which is on by default).
texts.setting.pistolstart.about: Starts every level from nothing, with no weapons or items kept from earlier levels. Health is also reset to 100%.
texts.setting.preventgameend.about: The triggers that end the game have no effect. This is useful for debugging, optimising and scripted play. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.preventlevelexit.about: Level exits have no effect. This is useful for debugging, optimising and scripted play. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.renderwipescreen.about: Turns on the screen melt, the effect shown when Doom changes scene, for example when a level starts or ends. The original game cannot turn it off. Its frames are lag frames, in which the game waits.
texts.setting.reportsecrets.about: Shows a message on screen when a secret is found. The original game does not have this.
texts.setting.rngseed.about: The starting value (seed) of the game's random number generator. It is used only for compatibility level 7 (Boom) and above. The default value is 1993.
texts.setting.scalefactor.about: The number the internal resolution is multiplied by (1 to 12). The picture looks sharper but is less faithful to the original. The original game's resolution is 320x200, stretched to a 4:3 shape on a CRT monitor. The core's picture is at most 3840x2400, so the widescreen shapes go up to 5.
texts.setting.sfxvolume.about: The volume of the sound effects (0 to 15).
texts.setting.showmessages.about: Shows messages about the items you pick up. The original game's default is "ON".
texts.setting.skilllevel.about: The difficulty. The original game defaults to 'Hurt me plenty', but 'Ultra-Violence' is the usual standard today.
texts.setting.solonet.about: Plays a single player as a network game (DSDA-Doom's -solo-net option), which the footer of a demo may ask for. A game with more than one player is a network game anyway.
texts.setting.spechitaddress.about: The memory address that the emulation of the spechit overflow assumes (DSDA-Doom's -spechit option), which the footer of a demo may give. 0 means the address in doom2.exe (0x01C09C98).
texts.setting.strafe50turns.about: The "Strafe" key is needed to turn a turning movement into the fastest sideways movement (strafe50). Without it the largest sideways value is 40. So with a keyboard and a mouse it is impossible to turn during strafe50. If strafe50 together with turning appears in a demo, the game accepts it, which makes it possible only in a tool-assisted run. This setting can turn it off for the most authentic behaviour.
texts.setting.turbo.about: Changes the player's running and sideways speed (0 to 255). -1 means it is off.
texts.setting.turningresolution.about: 'Shorttics' is the reduced turning precision normally used for demos. 'Longtics' is the normal turning precision outside demo recording. Newer demo formats support both.
texts.slot.pwad.help: The WADs (.wad) and DeHackEd patches (.deh, .bex) of the mod, in the order they are loaded. Where two WADs hold the same lump, the later one wins. Give none to play the game itself.
